1937年3月16日。

《每日新闻》

日本铜币走私者被捕

昨日，一名日本人在试图将铜币走私登上“长崎丸”号轮船时被中国海关官员发现，随后被日本领事警察逮捕。

日本领事警察查明，一些日本人从长崎来到上海，目的是走私铜币。对此，日本领事警察第一课课长田岛先生表示，必须逮捕那些从日本来此从事走私活动的人，因为担心此类活动可能引发其他犯罪。

日本军舰动向

日本巡洋舰“莲”号（Hasu）和“樫”号（Tsuga）昨日从日本抵达上海。炮舰“势多”号（Seta）将于明晨前往长江上游。第11舰队旗舰“安宅”号（Ataka）将于3月19日离开上海前往日本。巡洋舰“八重山”号（Yaeyama）将于今晨从日本抵达上海，并接替“安宅”号担任旗舰职责。

第11舰队司令谷本少将将于3月18日乘坐其旗舰离开上海进行巡视。

《日日新闻》

日本居留民团评议会

日本居留民团团长天野先生将于3月17日中午在日本俱乐部召集居留民团评议员会议，并就日本人选进入工部局（S.M.C.）的问题作全面报告。会议还将审议选举中日本候选人的遴选事宜。

《尼波报》（Nippo）

中日关系

《尼波报》发表如下评论：

3月14日，当地一家主要中文报纸刊登了一篇由一名叫周宪文（Chow Hsien Vung，音译）的中国人撰写的文章，该文涉及经济合作主题，并致

pages.en:
March 16, 1937.

-2-

to the Japanese economic mission. The article
represents the general view of the Chinese people.
It points out that China's purchasing of Japan's
industrial products and her selling of raw material
to Japan will tend to make her a Japanese colony.
For this reason, Sino-Japanese economic co-operation
will not be good for China. Chinese industrial
development will naturally lead to less buying of
Japanese goods. The author strongly advocates
that , to improve economic relations, Japan should
return Manchukuo to China, dissolve the East Hopei auto-
nomous government and suppress the smuggling activities
in the North, otherwise the two countries will remain
enemies.

We find that the object of
the Japanese economic mission and the efforts of some
prominent Chinese to bring about Sino-Japanese economic
co-operation have been grossly disregarded by the author
of the article whose motive apparently is to create
bad relations between the two countries. The author
says that when China's industrial state improves,
economic relations between her and Japan will de-
teriorate and Japanese goods will be boycotted in
this country. He seems to forget that good relations
still exist between Japan and other countries whose
industries are in a highly developed condition. We
ask the author, who is responsible for the establishment
of Manchukuo and the East Hopei autonomous government?
The Chinese government and the Chang regime which
ill-treated the people in Manchuria and East Hopei are
responsible. The people of Manchuria and East Hopei
organized their own governments and Japan has nothing
to do with them. The Manchukuo government and the
East Hopei Autonomous Government will never be dissolved
unless their people are willing to accept the Nanking
Government. It is rather ridiculous to ask Japan
to return Manchukuo to China and to dissolve the East
Hopei Autonomous Government, although it is true that
Japan pays serious attention to affairs in Manchukuo
and East Hopei because the situation there affects
her interests. The Chinese request to Japan to
suppress smuggling activities in North China is a
contemptuous one as the territory is under the control
of the Chinese authorities. The Chinese should ask
themselves who are the people who encourage such
activities by purchasing smuggled goods.

There are certain Powers which
ignore the principle of economic equality in China.
We ask the Chinese people not to obstruct Sino-Japanese
rapprochement.

1937年3月16日。

日本经济代表团。这篇文章代表了中国民众的一般观点。文章指出，中国购买日本的工业产品并向日本出售原材料，往往会使其成为日本的殖民地。因此，中日经济合作对中国不利。中国工业的发展自然会导致对日本商品购买的减少。作者强烈主张，为了改善经济关系，日本应将满洲国归还中国，解散冀东自治政府，并遏制北方的走私活动，否则两国将继续处于敌对状态。

我们发现，日本经济代表团的目标以及一些知名中国人士为促进中日经济合作所做的努力，被文章作者严重忽视，其动机显然是要破坏两国关系。作者称，当中国的工业状况改善时，其与日本的经济关系将恶化，日本商品将在本国遭到抵制。他似乎忘记了，日本与其他工业高度发达的国家之间仍保持着良好关系。我们要问作者，是谁负责建立满洲国和冀东自治政府？应对此负责的是中国政府以及在满洲和冀东虐待人民的张氏政权。满洲和冀东的人民组织了自己的政府，日本与此无关。除非其人民愿意接受南京政府，否则满洲国政府和冀东自治政府绝不会解散。要求日本将满洲国归还中国并解散冀东自治政府是相当荒谬的，尽管日本确实密切关注满洲和冀东的事务，因为那里的局势影响其利益。中国要求日本遏制华北的走私活动是一种蔑视性的要求，因为该地区处于中国当局的控制之下。中国人应该自问，是谁通过购买走私货物来鼓励此类活动。

某些列强无视在华经济平等原则。我们呼吁中国人民不要阻碍中日修好。

March 16, 1937. Afternoon Translation.

China Times published on March 14 the following special article written by Huang Yien Bei (黄炎培) :-

TO THE JAPANESE ECONOMIC MISSION

A Japanese Economic Mission, headed by Mr. Kenji Kodama, is now in China. Before the Mission left Tokyo, Mr. Kodama issued a statement to the effect that the object of the Mission was to look into the financial and economic reconstruction being undertaken by the Chinese Government and people, to exchange views on various subjects, and to strive to eradicate the unpleasant feelings existing between the peoples of Japan and China. We honestly believe that Mr. Kodama made this statement in all sincerity, and wish to take this opportunity to give him and his companions our opinions on the matter.

It is an undeniable fact that unpleasant relations do exist between the peoples of Japan and China. We once told a Japanese friend that to get at the root of the Sino-Japanese problem, one needed only to note the change in the Chinese people's affection for Japan after the May 9 and the September 18 Incidents. No one can remove the unpleasantness between the two peoples when the territory of the one is being occupied and its people oppressed by the other.

We wish Mr. Kodama and the members of the Mission would ascertain for themselves whether the present unpleasantness is the limit to which the Chinese people will go. Of all things, the Japanese hate to hear the expression "resistance to Japan"; yet Japan is working day and night to give rise to this resistance. She is enlarging the area of occupied territory and is oppressing the Chinese people, with the result that this expression is so deeply engraved in the hearts of all Chinese people that it will be impossible to efface it.

As regards financial and economic reconstruction, we would wish plainly to inform Mr. Kodama and the Mission that industrial and commercial circles and the financial authorities of China, in carrying out the work of financial and economic reconstruction, are being seriously hampered by one thing: smuggling. We will quote a passage from an article written by a foreigner, Mr. Haldore Hanson, published in the Pacific Affairs Monthly, Vol. 9, Issue 4 :-

"Future historians will record as a queer national policy the semi-official smuggling that is being carried out in North China by Japan in 1935-6. Under the constant protection of the Kwantung Army (the Japanese armed force in Manchuria), the Imperial Navy, the Gaimusho and the Japanese Consulates in China, a group of adventurous Koreans and Japanese broke down 150 miles of Chinese Customs barriers, and smuggled into China huge quantities of sugar and cotton cloth, rayon sufficient to make millions of socks and cigarette paper enough to provide every Chinese adult and child with one cigarette. Smuggled goods are transported with from ten to thirty motor boats from Dairen, through the North Chihli Bay where all obstructions have been removed by the Japanese Navy, and landed on the east

《字林西报》（China Times）于3月14日刊登了黄炎培先生撰写的以下特约文章：-

致日本经济考察团

由儿玉谦次先生率领的日本经济考察团目前正在中国。在该团离开东京之前，儿玉先生发表声明称，该团的目的是调查中国政府及人民正在进行的财政与经济重建工作，就各种议题交换意见，并努力消除中日两国人民之间存在的不良情绪。我们真诚地相信，儿玉先生的这一声明是出于诚意，并希望借此机会向他及其同伴陈述我们要对此事的看法。

中日两国人民之间存在不良关系，这是一个不可否认的事实。我们曾对一位日本朋友说，要探究中日问题的根源，只需注意“五九”国耻日和“九一八”事变后中国人民对日本感情的变化即可。当一方的领土被另一方占领、其人民受其压迫时，没有人能消除两国民众之间的不快。

我们希望儿玉先生及考察团成员亲自查明，目前的不快是否已是中国民众忍耐的极限。日本人最不愿听到的字眼莫过于“抗日”；然而，日本却日夜制造这种抵抗。日本不断扩大占领区并压迫中国人民，结果导致“抗日”一词深深铭刻在所有中国人的心中，无法抹去。

关于财政与经济重建，我们要明确告知儿玉先生及考察团，中国工商界和金融当局在开展财政与经济重建工作时，正受到一件事的严重阻碍：走私。我们将引用哈尔多尔·汉森（Haldore Hanson）先生发表在《太平洋事务月刊》（Pacific Affairs Monthly）第9卷第4期上的一篇文章中的一段话：-

“未来的历史学家将把1935-1936年间日本在华北进行的半官方走私记录为一种奇特的国家政策。在关东军（日本在满洲的武装力量）、帝国海军、外务省以及日本驻华领事馆的不断庇护下，一群冒险的朝鲜人和日本人突破了150英里长的中国海关防线，向中国走私了大量白糖和棉布，足以制作数百万双袜子的 rayon（人造丝），以及足够每个中国成人和儿童分得一支香烟的卷烟纸。走私货物由十至三十艘摩托艇从大连运出，穿过日本海军已清除所有障碍的北直隶湾，并在河北东海岸登陆，

pages.en:
March 16, 1937.
4
Afternoon Translation.

coast of Hopei either with the consent or the direct
assistance of the Japanese Consular Police. The goods
are then shipped to Tientsin by the Peiping Liaoning
Railway under the protection of Koreans. They arrive
at Tientsin every day at twenty minutes to noon when
thousands of Chinese coolies engaged by Japanese
merchants are ready to unload them from the trains.
These things are done with no more secrecy than the
ringing of a fire alarm."

According to a list compiled by Mr. Hanson,
this smuggling caused the Customs a loss of 19,120,000 gold
units in Custom duties for the period from August 1, 1935
to 1936. Mr. Hanson said that those which suffered most
were the Chinese sugar, cotton and rayon trades.
What reactions must these losses have created
in the minds of the Chinese financial authorities and Chinese
merchants? If a nation wants prosperity it must co-operate
with other nations. Owing to the geographical position of
the two countries, Japan should be the first country with
which China would seek co-operation; and if China, because of
the irregularity of her relations with Japan, should look
elsewhere for friends, who would be to blame?
Has not Mr. Kodama said that China's territorial
rights should be respected? The occupation of the Four
Eastern Provinces is followed by complications in North
China, and it is then said that "special circumstances"
exist there. If this phrase is accepted, what other names
may we not see invented?
I hope Mr. Kodama and his companions will pay a
visit to Chapei, where the shell-torn walls left by the war
of five years ago still can be seen. Perhaps, also,
Mr. Kodama and the members of the Mission will be able to
hear in their rooms at midnight the reports of firearms
discharged in the manoeuvres held in the vicinity of
Tien Tung An, these reports being usually loud enough to
arouse residents from their slumbers.
I sincerely hope that Mr. Kodama will work to
improve the relations between the peoples of Japan and China
on a basis of mutual benefit and reciprocity.
Various circles in Shanghai recently refused an
invitation to participate in the Pan-Pacific Exhibition at
Nagoya because there was a "Manchukuoan" Department in the
Exhibition.

下午译文。

此举要么得到了日本领事警察的同意，要么得到了他们的直接
协助。随后，这些货物在朝鲜人的保护下，经平宁铁路
运往天津。它们每天在中午11点40分抵达天津，届时
日本商人雇佣的数千名中国苦力已准备好从火车上卸货。
这些行径的公开程度，不亚于火警铃声。”

根据汉森先生编制的清单，
此次走私导致海关在1935年8月1日至1936年期间
损失关税19,120,000金单位。汉森先生称，遭受损失最重
的是中国的糖业、棉花和人造丝贸易。
这些损失在中国金融当局和中国
商人心中必然引起何种反应？如果一个国家想要繁荣，就必须
与其他国家合作。鉴于两国的地理位置，日本本应
是中国寻求合作的第一个国家；如果中国因与日本
关系不正常而另寻友邦，这又该怪谁呢？
儿玉先生不是说过应当尊重中国的领土
主权吗？东北四省的沦陷之后，华北又出现复杂局势，
随后便称那里存在“特殊情况”。如果接受这种说法，
我们还会看到其他什么名目被发明出来呢？
我希望儿玉先生及其同伴能去闸北看一看，那里
仍能看到五年前战争留下的弹痕累累的墙壁。或许，
儿玉先生及考察团成员还能在午夜时分，在他们的房间里
听到天通庵（Tien Tung An，音译）附近举行军事演习时
发出的枪声，这些枪声通常足以将居民从睡梦中惊醒。
我真诚希望儿玉先生能在互利互惠的基础上，
致力于改善中日两国人民之间的关系。
上海各界最近拒绝参加在名古屋举行的泛太平洋博览会
的邀请，因为博览会上设有“满洲国”馆。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, MONDAY, MARCH 15, 1937

ECONOMIC MISSION FROM
JAPAN ARRIVES
The arrival in Shanghai yesterday
afternoon of a strong Japanese Economic
Mission, headed by Mr. Kenji Kodama,
the internationally known banker, may or
may not result in any concrete improve-
ment in economic relations between
China and Japan but it should certainly
serve to clear the air and show how the
ground lies. We have had previous com-
mercial missions from Japan land on
these shores but the present is certainly
the most influential, containing as it does
some of Japan's leading and most success-
ful industrialists. Contrary to the
opinions of some people, we do not believe
that the improvement of the trade of any
one foreign nation with China must
necessarily militate against the success of
the others, provided—but this is a very
important proviso—that China's own
economy is improved at the same time.
If the vast population of China were
making the best economically of their
extensive country there would be enorm-
ous scope for trade with all the major
foreign States and there would be little
need for jealousy between them as to who
was making the most progress in a
market usually regarded as difficult. We
believe, too, that the improvement of
China's economy has already set in and,
if there should be no war or major
calamity to hinder it, that there will be
no going back in the future. It is
believed unlikely that the present
Economic Mission from Japan will make
any concrete proposals for extensive
Sino-Japanese economic co-operation in
the immediate future but rather that it
will endeavour to explore conditions as
much as possible and seek to "get in
touch" as closely as possible with import-
ant Chinese commercial interests. The
Mission is proceeding at once to Nanking
where its members will be given a good
reception by official, banking and com-
mercial circles. The commerce between
China and Japan has recently shown an
upward tendency and there is no doubt
that it could continue to do so without
doing damage to other foreign interests.
There are indications already that China's
financial and economic strengthening are
likely to make considerable strides for-
ward before the end of the year and there
are hopes that this will lead to a larger
and more profitable foreign trade for all
concerned. It is possible that 1937 will
be a real turning-point in this respect but
it must be recognized that a number of
years must elapse before China takes her
rightful place in the economy of nations.
The disorganization of decades cannot be
overcome immediately despite the strenu-
ous efforts of the Nanking Government.
Meanwhile, it will be to the benefit of all
if politics are kept out of the way as much
as possible.

S-1.
DBR
JB 15/3/73

《上海泰晤士报》，1937年3月15日，星期一

日本经济考察团抵沪

由国际知名银行家儿玉谦次先生率领的强大日本经济
考察团于昨日下午抵达上海。此举能否切实改善中
日之间的经济关系尚难断言，但无疑有助于澄清气氛，
表明事态现状。此前曾有日本商业代表团登陆此间，
但本次代表团无疑是最具影响力的，其中包含日本一些
领先且最成功的实业家。与某些人的观点相反，我们
并不认为任何一个外国国家对华贸易的改善必然
会损害其他国家的成功，前提是——这是一个非常
重要的前提——中国的自身经济同时得到改善。
如果中国庞大的人口能够对其广袤国土进行最佳的经济
利用，那么与所有主要外国国家的贸易将有巨大的
空间，各国也就无需在这个通常被视为困难的市场中
嫉妒谁取得了最大进展。我们也相信，中国经济的
改善已经开始，如果没有战争或重大灾难加以阻
碍，未来将不可逆转。人们认为，目前的日本经济
考察团不太可能在近期提出任何关于广泛中日经济
合作的具体建议，而是将尽力探查情况，并力求
与中国重要商业利益集团尽可能紧密地“建立联系”。
考察团随即前往南京，其成员将受到官方、银行界和商
界的热烈欢迎。近期中日贸易呈现上升趋势，毫
无疑问，这种趋势可以在不损害其他外国利益的情况
下持续下去。已有迹象表明，中国的财政和经济实力
有望在年底前取得长足进步，人们希望这将使所有相
关方获得更大且更有利可图的对外贸易。1937年有
可能成为这方面的一个真正转折点，但必须认识到，
在中国在国际经济中占据其应有地位之前，还需经过
数年时光。尽管南京政府付出了巨大努力，数十年的
混乱局面不可能立即克服。
与此同时，如果尽可能排除政治干扰，将对各方都有利。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, MONDAY, MARCH 15, 1937

MISSION TO STUDY TRADE
OF CHINA AND JAPAN

Leading Japanese Business Men Arrive in Shanghai to
Confer with Nanking

MET AT THE WHARF BY MANY OFFICIALS

Representatives of Chief Industrial Cities of the Island
Empire Included in Group

FOURTEEN of Japan's leading bankers, industrialists and shippers arrived here yesterday afternoon for a series of conferences with Chinese businessmen and officials of the Nanking Government.

A large crowd greeted the Japanese mission when the ss. Nagasaki Maru tied up at the Wayside Wharf of the Nippon Yusen Kaisha. Included among them were: Mr. Tatsuo Kawai, Japanese Consul-General; representatives of the local Japanese community; Mr. Chou Tso-min, President of the Kingcheng Banking Corporation and Chairman of the Sino-Japanese Trade Association; and Mr. Hsu Shih-ying, Ambassador to Tokyo.

Mr. Kenji Kodama, head of the mission and former President of the Yokohama Specie Bank, declined to make a detailed statement on the aims and hopes of the group.

"We came here at the invitation of the Sino-Japanese Trade Association, and have no special mission to perform.

"I am very pleased at having an opportunity to meet here some of my old acquaintances, whom I have not seen in seventeen years."

Mr. Kodama once served in Shanghai as the manager of the local branch of the Yokohama Specie Bank.

Immediately after landing, the mission made calls of courtesy at the Japanese Consulate-General; on Vice-Admiral Kiyoshi Hasegawa, Commander of the Third Fleet, aboard his flagship the cruiser Idzumo; and on Rear-Admiral Koshiro Kondo, Commander of the Special Landing Party.

In the evening, the members of the mission were the guests of honour at a banquet given by leading local residents at the Japanese Club.

At 11 o'clock last night, they boarded a special car attached to the Nanking-bound train. On their arrival at the Capital this morning, the group will face a busy programme of interviews with Government officials and various formal functions.

Members of Party

In addition to Mr. Kodama, the mission included: Mr. Noboru Ohtani, President of the Nippon Yusen Kaisha; Mr. Keizaburo Kato President of the Bank of Chosen; Mr. Hyakutaro Miyakegawa, adviser to the Mitsubishi Trading Company; Mr. Seijiro Miyajima, President of the Nisshin Cotton Textile Company and Mr. Reisuke Ishida, managing director of the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha.

Other representatives of the Tokyo business world were: Mr. Shin Hori, President of the Nisshin Kisen Kaisha; Mr. Ikuki Akiyama, adviser to the Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha; Mr. Alichiro Fujiyama, President of the Nippon Sugar Company; and Mr. Kyoichi Aburatani, director of the Sino-Japanese Trade Association.

Osaka Men

Osaka is represented on the mission by Mr. Otokichi Shoji, President of the Tokyo Cotton Textile Company and Chairman of the Dai-Nippon Cotton Textile Association; Mr. Kensaku Ohira, managing director of the Sumitomo Bank, and Mr. Ichiji Iio, President of the Dong Shing Spinning and Weaving Company.

Nagoya is represented on the mission by Mr. Risaburo Toyoda, President of the Toyoda Cotton Spinning and Weaving Company.

The mission is accompanied by a suite of seven.

Among others greeting the mission upon its arrival were Mr. Chow Chueh, Director of the Shanghai Office of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Messrs. Yu Ya-ching, Lin Kang-hou, Tu Yueh-sen, Y. M. Chien, and a large number of local industrial and commercial leaders.

Mr. Hsu to Resign

"I shall again tender my resignation from the post as Ambassador to Japan when I meet General Chiang Kai-shek," Mr. Hsu Shih-ying informed local pressmen at the Wayside Wharf yesterday when greeting the foreign-controlled area."

Mr. Hsu, who has just returned from Nanking where he reported on his duties to the Central Government and asked for approval of his resignation, said that his request had been rejected by Dr. Wang Chung-hui, Minister of Foreign Affairs, who earnestly asked him to carry on.

Prior to his return from Japan, Mr. Hsu said, he had tendered his resignation to the Central Government, but it was also rejected by Gen. Chang Chun, then foreign Minister.

Mr. Hsu accompanied the Japanese Mission to Nanking and will return to Shanghai on March 17 or 18.

《字林西报》，1937年3月15日，星期一

考察中日贸易代表团

日本商界领袖抵沪与南京方面会谈

众多官员前往码头迎接

代表团成员包括该岛国主要工业城市的代表

昨天下午，十四位日本顶尖银行家、实业家和船运商抵达此处，旨在与中国商人及南京政府官员举行一系列会议。

当“长崎丸”号（ss. Nagasaki Maru）停靠在日本邮船会社（Nippon Yusen Kaisha）的码头时，一大群民众迎接了日本代表团。迎接者中包括：日本总领事河相达夫（Tatsuo Kawai）先生；当地日侨社区代表；金城银行总裁兼中日贸易协会主席周作民（Chou Tso-min）先生；以及驻东京大使许世英（Hsu Shih-ying）先生。

代表团团长、前横滨正金银行总裁儿玉谦次（Kenji Kodama）先生拒绝对该团体的目标和希望发表详细声明。

“我们是应中日贸易协会的邀请来到这里的，并没有执行什么特殊使命。

“我很高兴有机会在这里会见一些我已十七年未见的老朋友。”

儿玉先生曾在上海担任横滨正金银行当地分行的经理。

登陆后，代表团立即进行了礼节性拜访，先后拜会了日本总领事馆；第三舰队司令长谷川清（Kiyoshi Hasegawa）海军中将，在其旗舰“出云”号巡洋舰上；以及特别陆战队指挥官近藤信竹（Koshiro Kondo）海军少将。

当晚，代表团成员作为主宾，出席了当地知名人士在日本俱乐部举行的宴会。

昨晚11时，他们登上了附挂在开往南京列车后的专用车厢。今晨抵达首都后，该团体将面临繁忙的日程，包括与政府官员的面谈以及各种正式活动。

代表团成员

除儿玉先生外，代表团成员还包括：日本邮船会社总裁大谷登（Noboru Ohtani）先生；朝鲜银行总裁加藤惠三郎（Keizaburo Kato）先生；三菱商事顾问三宅川百太郎（Hyakutaro Miyakegawa）先生；日清纺织公司总裁宫岛诚次郎（Seijiro Miyajima）先生；以及三井物产常务董事石田礼助（Reisuke Ishida）先生。

来自东京商界的其他代表有：日清汽船株式会社总裁堀真（Shin Hori）先生；三菱合资公司顾问秋山育树（Ikuki Akiyama）先生；日本制糖公司总裁藤山爱一郎（Alichiro Fujiyama）先生；以及中日贸易协会理事阿部谷恭一（Kyoichi Aburatani）先生。

大阪方面代表

大阪在代表团中的代表有：东京棉业纺织公司总裁、大日本棉纺织同业公会会长庄司乙吉（Otokichi Shoji）先生；住友银行常务董事大平贤作（Kensaku Ohira）先生；以及东兴纺绩织布公司总裁饭尾一次（Ichiji Iio）先生。

名古屋在代表团中的代表有：丰田棉纺绩织布公司总裁丰田利三郎（Risaburo Toyoda）先生。

代表团随行人员共七人。

其他在抵达时迎接代表团的人士包括：外交部上海办事处主任卓觉（Chow Chueh，音译）先生，虞洽卿（Yu Ya-ching）、林康侯（Lin Kang-hou）、杜月笙（Tu Yueh-sen）、钱永铭（Y. M. Chien）等先生，以及众多本地工商业领袖。

许氏拟辞职

“当我见到蒋介石将军时，我将再次提出辞去驻日本大使职务，”许世英先生昨天在码头迎接来自外国管制区域的人士时向当地记者表示。

许先生刚从南京返回，他在那里向中央政府汇报工作并请求批准其辞呈。他说，他的请求已被外交部长王宠惠博士拒绝，王部长恳切要求他留任。

许先生称，在从日本回国之前，他曾向中央政府提出辞职，但同样被时任外交部长的张群将军拒绝。

许先生将陪同日本代表团前往南京，并将于3月17日或18日返回上海。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, MONDAY, MARCH 15, 1937

MISSION FROM JAPAN

The influential economic Mission which has been sent from Japan to China is thoroughly representative of the banking, business and industrial life of Japan. Probably no more important body of commercial men has ever visited this country from across the Yellow Sea. It should give an authoritative touch to the movement for Sino-Japanese economic co-operation and it therefore comes with special appropriateness just when the new Japanese Foreign Minister has reaffirmed his Government's desire to approach the cementing of ties of friendship with China on the basis of a mutual regard for the economic and financial interests of the two countries whose interdependence, politically and economically, is so self-evident. In the light of political relationships as developed during the last six years, it will be recognized that the Mission has no easy task. Indeed, Mr. Naotake Sato is already finding his own statement of policy challenged by powerful elements in the fighting services and, although supported by General Senjuro Hayashi and General Gen Sugiyama, the Prime Minister and the War Minister respectively, he has yet to obtain the Privy Council's endorsement of his views. This is not surprising for the course of events in North China alone in recent years has created conditions which, unless profoundly modified, are incompatible with that regard for China's sovereignty to which Mr. Sato seemed to give impeccable definition. The Mission which now seeks to establish a workable economic understanding with China is bound to be confronted by the same difficulties. Solution is not impossible but unless the "new concept" which Japanese statesmen have lately talked of applying to their country's relations with China is an empty phrase, it cannot be readily discerned without some remedial treatment of Chinese grievances as specially subsisting in the so-called autonomy of East Hopei, the smuggling threat to China's service of her foreign loan services and the present disabilities experienced by Chinese authority in making military dispositions in Chinese territory in the North.

It has been hinted that the Mission may be prepared to recognize the need for withdrawing Japanese support of the East Hopei smuggling paradise—on which further light is thrown by the Government's publication to-day of another of Sir Frederick Maze's routine periodical reports—on condition that the Chinese authorities carry out a downward revision of their tariff. In tackling the question of economic co-operation it may also be proposed that Japanese Banks, following at last the example of other foreign banks, should hand over their silver holdings, estimated at about $9 million, provided that the money is placed at the disposal of a scheme for development of railways and other undertakings in North China. Thus Chinese money would be applied by Japanese pressure to beneficent enterprises which have for some time past been regarded as of special importance to Japanese interests in the North. Viewed in that light it will be agreed that such proposals will require considerable diplomatic agility for commendation to China's favourable attention. In themselves, if thus correctly defined, they are highly satisfactory, but it is difficult to see how they can find acceptance in the setting devised for them. It will be recognized that the Chinese Government carries a responsibility as precisely defined last month by the Fifth Central Executive Committee at its Third Plenary Session:

In our external relations we shall not tolerate any aggression against our territorial sovereignty...... If there is still hope for peace we shall still be willing to continue our efforts in working for a preliminary readjustment of Sino-Japanese relations on the basis of equality reciprocity and mutual respect of each other's territory.

Japanese diplomacy will perceive that this obligation duly accepted by the Government cannot be ignored in the discussions likely to emerge from the visit of the eminent business men at whose head stands

Mr. Kenji Kodama, formerly President of the Yokohama Specie Bank.

Political changes in Japan have firmly brought the influence of men like Mr. Kodama again into the picture. General Hayashi depends in no small degree on the benevolent support of industrialists and bankers who are in close sympathy with the politicians' demand for a proper control of the militarists. It is probable therefore that the Kodama Mission will not blindly accept the prescription provided by militarist interpretation of the Hirota policy, especially as Mr. Sato himself—with General Hayashi's implicit approval —has frankly demanded latitude in endorsing its "three points." First things, Nanking may say, must come first. Political issues have to be clarified before economic problems can be pressed to solution. Or, putting it in another way, it is inconsistent with the principle of equality that economic proposals should be based on the conditional rectification of breaches of China's sovereignty. Nor does it seem consonant with Japan's dignity to claim that support which should never have been given to the smugglers of the North cannot be withdrawn unless China adopts a downward revision of her tariff. This flagrantly would infringe her tariff autonomy guaranteed to her by solemn treaty. It is conceivable that China will be prepared to consider specific tariff rates which are held to operate unfairly against Japanese imports, but the issue can hardly be linked with the restoration of China's clear rights to prevent smuggling without gravely prejudicing the fundamental character of equal negotiation. If the "new concept" of which Mr. Shigeru Kawagoe and his chief at the Foreign Office have so insistently spoken has reality, these points are likely to receive attention. So, too, are the conditions in which Chinese authority in Hopei and Charhar is being subjected to Japanese military supervision. The whole question is, of course, exclusively the concern of Japan and China, as they develop the admirable purpose of ending an unsatisfactory impasse. It comes within the purview of outside commentary only in so far as it has to be taken into account in assessing the possible trend of the discussions which the Kodama Mission is expected to initiate on its arrival at Nanking. Everyone interested in the stabilization of Far Eastern affairs will wish the Mission success, but it would be doing no service to either party if the essentials of a permanent and practicable agreement were glossed over or if vital principles of international comity were treated as negligible.

《字林西报》，1937年3月15日，星期一

来自日本的代表团

此次从日本派往中国的具有影响力的经济代表团，充分代表了日本的银行业、商业和工业生活。或许从未有如此重要的商界团体跨越黄海访问过这个国家。这将为中日经济合作运动赋予权威的基调，因此，正值新任日本外相重申其政府希望在相互尊重两国经济和金融利益的基础上加强友好纽带之际，该代表团的到来显得尤为恰当。两国的相互依赖在政治和经济上都是不言而喻的。鉴于过去六年发展起来的政治关系，人们会认识到，代表团的任务并不轻松。事实上，佐藤尚武（Naotake Sato）先生已经发现他的政策声明受到军界强大势力的挑战，尽管他得到了首相林铣十郎（Senjuro Hayashi）将军和陆军大臣杉山元（Gen Sugiyama）将军的支持，但他尚未获得枢密院对其观点的认可。这并不令人惊讶，因为仅近年来华北的事态发展就造成了除非得到深刻改变、否则与佐藤先生似乎给予完美阐释的对中国主权的尊重不相容的条件。现在寻求与中国建立可行的经济谅解的代表团必然面临同样的困难。解决并非不可能，但如果日本政治家最近谈论的要应用于其对华关系的“新概念”不是一句空话，那么如果不针对中国特别存在的 grievances（不满/冤屈）采取某些补救措施——特别是所谓冀东自治、走私对中国偿还外债服务的威胁，以及中国当局在北方中国领土上进行军事部署目前所遭受的限制——就很难轻易看出这一概念的内涵。

有人暗示，如果中国当局下调关税，代表团可能准备承认需要撤回日本对冀东走私天堂的支持——政府今天公布了梅乐和爵士（Sir Frederick Maze）的另一份例行定期报告，进一步揭示了这一点——在处理经济合作问题时，还可能提议日本银行最终效仿其他外国银行的榜样，交出估计约为900万元的白银持有量，前提是将这笔资金用于华北铁路开发和其他事业计划。这样，在中国资金将在日本的压力下被用于那些长期以来被认为对日本在华北利益特别重要的有益企业。从这个角度来看，人们会同意，此类提案需要相当高的外交技巧才能赢得中国的青睐。就其本身而言，如果这样正确定义，它们是令人非常满意的，但很难看出它们如何在为其设计的背景下被接受。人们会认识到，中国政府承担着上个月第五届中央执行委员会第三次全体会议明确规定的责任：

在对外关系中，我们不容忍任何侵犯我国领土主权的行为……如果和平仍有希望，我们仍愿意继续努力，在平等互惠和相互尊重各自领土的基础上，初步调整中日关系。

日本外交界将意识到，在由儿玉谦次先生（前横滨正金银行总裁）为首的杰出商界人士访问可能引发的讨论中，不能忽视政府 duly accepted（正式承担）的这一义务。

日本的政治变革已使像儿玉先生这样的人物的影响力重新回到视野中。林将军在很大程度上依赖于实业家和银行家的善意支持，这些人与政客们要求适当控制军阀势力的诉求有着密切的共鸣。因此，儿玉代表团很可能不会盲目接受军国主义对广田政策的解释所提供的方案，尤其是佐藤先生本人——在林将军的默许下——已坦率要求在认可其“三点”时拥有回旋余地。南京方面可能会说，首要之事必须优先处理。在推动解决经济问题之前，必须先澄清政治问题。或者换一种说法，如果经济提案是基于有条件地纠正对中国主权的侵犯，这就与平等原则不一致。声称除非中国下调关税，否则无法撤回本就不应给予北方走私者的支持，这似乎也不符合日本的尊严。这将公然侵犯庄严条约保证给中国的关税自主权。可以设想，中国将准备考虑被认为对日本进口商品运作不公的具体关税税率，但如果不严重损害平等谈判的基本性质，这一问题很难与恢复中国防止走私的明确权利联系起来。如果川越茂（Shigeru Kawagoe）先生及其外务省上司如此坚持谈论的“新概念”具有现实性，这些要点可能会受到关注。同样受到关注的还有河北和察哈尔的中国当局受到日本军事监督的状况。当然，整个问题 exclusively（完全）是日本和中国的事情，因为他们致力于结束这种令人不满的僵局的 admirable purpose（良好愿望）。只有当评估儿玉代表团抵达南京后预期发起的讨论的可能趋势时，它才属于外部评论的范围。所有关心远东事务稳定的人都希望代表团取得成功，但如果掩盖永久且可行协议的本质，或将国际礼让的重要原则视为微不足道，将对任何一方都无益。

pages.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Monday, March 15, 1937

Japan's Trade Visitors
JAPAN'S VISITING economic group has received a deservedly warm welcome. It represents a type of penetration into China to which none can take exception so long as its tactics are on the "open door" basis indicated— a refreshing contrast to policies of penetration behind the point of the bayonet.
Perhaps it is excess of optimism to lump this mission, the recent praiseworthy remarks of Foreign Minister Naotake Sato, and certain improvements in the North China situation together as representing a complete change of heart on the part of Japan. There are and have been numerous differences of opinion among the Japanese as to the best way to deal with China, and it is only to be expected that divided councils will continue in some degree.
But we are convinced that not only Japan but any other country will profit economically far more by giving China a square deal than by striving to dominate her against her will. That is a moderate and we believe a fair statement, to which such men as our present visitors will no doubt wholeheartedly subscribe.
In addition to cultivating Chinese friendship we trust that they will not miss this opportunity to meet other foreigners who seek trade in China, with the idea that it is to nobody's interest to indulge either in oppression toward China or in unfair or unprofitable competition toward each other. Better understanding of the whole problem should work for the betterment of all concerned.

S.I.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1937年3月15日，星期一

日本的贸易访客

日本来访的经济代表团受到了当之无愧的热烈欢迎。只要其策略基于所指的“门户开放”原则，这种对中国的渗透类型是无人能提出异议的，这与刺刀尖下的渗透政策形成了令人耳目一新的对比。

也许将此次出访、外相佐藤尚武最近值得称赞的言论以及华北局势的某些改善归结为日本方面的彻底转变，是过于乐观了。在日本人内部，关于处理中国问题的最佳方式一直存在且仍存在着许多意见分歧，因此决策层在某种程度上继续存在分歧也是意料之中的事。

但我们深信，不仅日本，任何其他国家若能公平对待中国，而非违背中国意愿试图支配她，将在经济上获得大得多的利益。这是一个温和且我们认为公正的陈述，像我们目前的访客这样的人无疑会全心全意地赞同。

除了培养与中国的友谊外，我们希望他们不要错过与其他寻求在华贸易的外国人会面的机会，秉持这样的理念：无论是压迫中国，还是彼此间进行不公平或无利可图的竞争，都不符合任何人的利益。对整个问题的更好理解应有助于改善所有相关方的处境。

S.I.

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Monday, March 15, 1937'

Nanking Greets
Japanese Party

Warmest Expressions
Of Hospitality
Since 1931

(Domei)
NANKING, Mar. 15.—China's capital today extended a warm welcome to the Japanese Economic Mission, led by Mr. Kenji Kodama, a former president of the Yokohama Specie Bank, as it arrived here for a two-day stay.
The elaborate arrangements and functions exceeded all Chinese expressions of hospitality towards Japanese visitors since the fall of 1931.
Mr. Wu Ting-chang, minister of Industry and leader of the Chinese mission to Japan in 1935, led an imposing delegation of Chinese officials who met the visitors at the station. Local Japanese officials, including Mr. Shigeru Kawagoe, Ambassador, were also on hand to greet the members of the mission.

Honor Sun Yat-sen
After breakfast at the Metropolitan Hotel, the group drove to the mausoleum of Dr. Sun Yat-sen, where they placed a wreath on the tomb of the father of the Chinese Republic.
Later in the morning, the Mission went on a series of courtesy calls on Dr. Lin Sen, President of the National Government; General Chiang Kai-shek, president of the Executive Yuan; Dr. Wang Ching-hui, Minister of Foreign Affairs; Dr. H. H. Kung, Minister of Finance; Mr. Chang Kia-ngau, Minister of Railways, and Mayor Ma Chao-chun.

Visit Wang's Home
A visit was also made to the home of Mr. Wang Ching-wei, chairman of the Central Political Council, who is now in Suiyuan.
Ambassador Kawagoe was host at a luncheon in the mission's honor at the Metropolitan Hotel at 12:30 o'clock noon. Attending the function were more than 40 Chinese government leaders including Dr. Kung, Dr. Wang, Mr. Wu, Gen. Chiang Tso-pin, Minister of the Interior, and Mr. Hsu Shih-ying, Ambassador to Japan.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1937年3月15日，星期一

南京欢迎
日本代表团

自1931年以来
最热烈的款待表示

（同盟社）
南京，3月15日电。——中国首都今天向日本经济代表团表示了热烈欢迎，该团由横滨正金银行前总裁儿玉谦次先生率领，抵达此处进行为期两天的访问。

其精心安排的接待和活动超过了自1931年秋季以来中方对日本访客的所有款待表示。

吴鼎昌部长（1935年赴日中国代表团团长）率领一支庞大的中国官员代表团在车站迎接访客。包括大使川越茂先生在内的当地日本官员也到场欢迎代表团成员。

谒见孙中山先生

在大都会饭店用早餐后，该团驱车前往孙中山博士陵墓，并在中华民国国父的墓前敬献花圈。

上午晚些时候，代表团依次拜会了国民政府主席林森博士、行政院院长蒋介石将军、外交部长王宠惠博士、财政部长孔祥熙博士、铁道部长张嘉璈先生以及市长马超俊先生。

拜访汪宅

代表团还拜访了中央政治委员会主席汪精卫先生的寓所，汪先生目前身在绥远。

中午12时30分，川越大使在大都会饭店设午宴招待代表团。出席活动的有40多位中国政府领导人，包括孔祥熙博士、王宠惠博士、吴鼎昌先生、内政部长蒋作宾将军以及驻日大使许世英先生。

March 15, 1937.
（印：GENERAL FILE C. A. REGISTRY No. D 006）

MALIONI

CHINESE ASSUMED CONTEMPTUOUS ATTITUDE TOWARDS JAPAN

The Mainichi publishes the following leading article:-
China has begun to assume a contemptuous attitude towards Japan as a result of the adoption of a new foreign policy by the Third Plenary Session and the modification of Japan's China policy by the Hayashi Cabinet. It has become apparent especially since the appointment of Mr. Sato as Foreign Minister. It is feared that China will adopt a stronger attitude towards Japan in the future.
It is the Chinese view that as regards internal political affairs the Third Plenary Session has decided to close the tutelage period and open a constitutional period owing to the fact that China's unification movement has been crowned with success. As regards economic affairs the Session has adopted a large constructive plan , as regards foreign policy it has decided to seek assistance from America, France and Soviet Russia for reconstruction. It is decided to maintain territorial integrity by making preparations for war against Japan , cutting down toleration of her oppression without necessarily irritating her. Great Britain's assistance to China played an important part in checking Japan's influence as well as in reconstructing China. Japan was attempting to establish a hegemony in China by overriding British influence, but the attempt has now ended in failure. Great Britain and China are closer than ever before. As a result Japan must alter her China policy. The advocation in Japan of Sino-Japanese economic co-operation is evidently an attempt to redress the failure of Japan's policy towards China, but it is unbelievable that Japan's fundamental policy towards China will be changed. The object of Japan's economic activities in China is the invasion of the country but that of Great Britain's is to reconstruct it. If Japan wishes to alter China's views about her she should cease her activities in the North and release various economic and political organizations in North China so that the Central Government will be able to control them. The question of Manchukuo could then be discussed.
It is only to be expected that Chinese government officials and the people who hold Japan responsible for the September 18 incident and do not know about the situation in North China would entertain such views on Japan. They are unable to see the situation clearly. Thus as soon as Japan changes her policy they assume a contemptuous attitude towards her.
Having received an unpleasant impression of the Chinese people through articles appearing in the Chinese press and through the speech delivered the other day by a Chinese guest at the entertainment given by the joint meeting of Japanese Chambers of Commerce in China, we publish this article with a view to assisting our economic mission now visiting China to obtain a correct viewpoint on the country.

MALIONI

中国人对日本表现出轻蔑态度

《每日新闻》发表以下社论：

由于三中全会采取新的外交政策以及林内阁修改对华政策，中国开始对日本表现出轻蔑态度。自从任命佐藤先生为外相以来，这一点变得尤为明显。人们担心中国未来会对日本采取更强硬的态度。

中方认为，就内部政治事务而言，鉴于中国的统一运动已取得圆满成功，三中全会决定结束训政时期，开启宪政时期。就经济事务而言，全会通过了一项大型建设计划；就外交政策而言，全会决定寻求美国、法国和苏俄的帮助以进行重建。会议决定通过对日备战来维护领土完整，在不必然激怒日本的情况下减少对其压迫的容忍。英国对中国的援助在遏制日本影响以及重建中国方面发挥了重要作用。日本曾试图通过压倒英国的影响来在中国建立霸权，但这一尝试现已以失败告终。英中关系比以往任何时候都更加紧密。因此，日本必须改变其对华政策。日本国内倡导中日经济合作，显然是为了纠正日本对华政策的失败，但令人难以置信的是日本对华根本政策会发生改变。日本在华经济活动的目的是侵略该国，而英国的目的则是重建该国。如果日本希望改变中国对她的看法，她应停止在华北的活动，并释放华北的各种经济和政治组织，以便中央政府能够控制它们。届时便可讨论满洲国问题。

那些将九一八事变归咎于日本且不了解华北局势的中国政府官员和民众持有上述对日观点，这是意料之中的事。他们无法看清局势。因此，一旦日本改变政策，他们便对日本表现出轻蔑态度。

鉴于通过中文报刊上的文章以及近日在中日商会联合会议上的一位中国宾客的演讲，我们对中国人民留下了不愉快的印象，我们发表此文，旨在协助目前正在访华的经济代表团获得对该国的正确观点。

THE KAYAU MURDER CASE

The eight accused in the
Kayau murder case were sentenced recently by the Shanghai
District Court. The accused filed an appeal with the
Kiangsu High Court against the judgement of the Court
of First Instance.

During the first and second

THE CHINA PRESS, MONDAY, MARCH 15, 1937

Japan Trade
Group Here
For Sessions

Mission Members Go
To Nanking Before
Opening Meetings

KODAMA HEADS
PARTY OF 13

Warm Welcome Given
By Chinese Business
Leaders

Thirteen of Japan's leading bankers, industrialists and shipping magnates, coming to China as a trade mission to seek economic co-operation with this country, arrived in Shanghai yesterday afternoon on board the Nagasaki Maru.
Members of the group, greeted at the wharf by a large delegation of Chinese and Japanese businessmen and officials, left here last night on a special coach for Nanking where they will today begin a busy schedule of calls on Government officials and attendance at various informal functions.
Greeting the visitors yesterday were Mr. Hsu Shih-ying, Chinese Ambassador to Japan; Mr. Chow Tso-ming, Chairman of the Sino-Japanese Trade Federation, Mr. Ling Kang-hou, Secretary-General of the Chinese Bankers' Association; Dr. P. W. Kuo, Director of the Bureau of Foreign Trade; Mr. Tu Yueh-sen, influential local businessman and others.
The Japanese mission was accompanied to Nanking last night by Ambassador Hsu and Mr. Chow.
Interviewed by pressmen, Mr. Kenji Kodama, head of the mission and former President of the Yokohama Specie Bank, declined to make a detailed statement regarding the aims and hopes of the group.

Denies Special Mission
Explaining that he had already outlined his plans to Tokyo correspondents, Mr. Kodama told reporters, however, that the mission came here at the invitation of the Sino-Japanese Trade Federation and has no special mission to perform.
"I am very pleased at having an opportunity to meet in Shanghai some of my old acquaintances whom I have not seen in 7 years," the veteran Japanese financier said.
Mr. Kodama once served as the manager of the Shanghai branch of the Yokohama Specie Bank.
Questioned by reporters whether he will go to North China, Mr. Kodama revealed that he will visit Shanghai and Nanking only. After attending the general meeting of the trade federation in Shanghai and renewing his contacts with local Chinese business leaders, he will return to Japan, he added.

Pay Courtesy Calls
Immediately after their arrival, members of the mission paid courtesy calls at the Japanese Consulate-General and on the various Japanese military and naval commands in Shanghai.
In the evening, the group were entertained by leading local Nipponese residents at the Japanese Club.
In addition to Mr. Kodama, the mission included: Mr. Keizaburo Kato, President of the Bank of Chosen; Mr. Hyakutaro Miyakegawa, adviser to the Mitsubishi Trading Company; Mr. Seijiro Miyajima, President of the Nisshin Cotton Textile Company, and Mr. Reisuke Ishida, managing director of the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha.
Other representatives of the Tokyo business world were: Mr. Shin Hori, President of the Nisshin Kisen Kaisha; Mr. Ikuki Akiyama, adviser to the Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha; Mr. Aiichiro Fujiyama, President of the Nippon Sugar Company, and Mr. Kyoichi Aburatani, director of the Sino-Japanese Trade Association.
Osaka is represented on the mission by Mr. Otokichi Shoji, President of the Tokyo Cotton Textile Company and Chairman of the Dai-Nippon Cotton Textile Association; Mr. Kensaku Ohira, managing director of the Sumitomo Bank, and Mr. Ichiji Iio, President of the Dong Shing Spinning and Weaving Company.
Nagoya is represented on the mission by Mr. Risaburo Toyoda, President of the Toyoda Cotton Spinning and Weaving Company.
The mission is accompanied by a suite of seven.

《字林西报》，1937年3月15日，星期一

日本贸易
代表团抵沪
参加会议

会议开幕前
代表团成员
前往南京

儿玉率领
13人代表团

中国商界领袖
给予热烈欢迎

十三位日本顶尖银行家、实业家和航运巨头作为寻求与本国进行经济合作的贸易代表团，于昨日下午乘坐长崎丸号抵达上海。

该团成员在码头受到大批中日商人和官员代表团的欢迎，昨晚乘专车离开此处前往南京，今天他们将开始繁忙的日程，拜会政府官员并参加各种非正式活动。

昨日迎接访客的有：中国驻日大使许世英先生、中日贸易联合会主席周作民先生、中国银行公会秘书长凌康侯先生、对外贸易局局长郭秉文博士、当地有影响力的商人杜月笙先生等其他人。

许大使和周先生昨晚陪同日本代表团前往南京。

面对记者的采访，代表团团长、横滨正金银行前总裁儿玉谦次先生拒绝对该团的目标和希望发表详细声明。

否认特殊使命

儿玉先生解释说，他已向驻东京记者概述了他的计划，但他告诉记者，该团是应中日贸易联合会的邀请而来，并无特殊使命要执行。

这位资深日本金融家说：“很高兴有机会在上海见到一些我七年未见的老朋友。”

儿玉先生曾任横滨正金银行上海分行经理。

当记者问他是否将前往华北时，儿玉先生透露他将只访问上海和南京。他补充说，在参加上海贸易联合会的全体会议并与当地中国商界领袖重新建立联系后，他将返回日本。

礼节性拜会

抵达后，代表团成员立即礼节性拜会了日本驻上海总领事馆以及上海各日本陆海军司令部。

晚上，当地主要日本居民在日本俱乐部宴请了该团。

除儿玉先生外，代表团成员还包括：朝鲜银行总裁加藤庆三郎先生、三菱商事公司顾问三宅川百太郎先生、日清纺织株式会社总裁宫岛诚二郎先生，以及三井物产株式会社常务理事石田礼助先生。

来自东京商界的其他代表有：日清汽船株式会社总裁堀新先生、三菱合资会社顾问秋山育树先生、日本制糖株式会社总裁藤山爱一郎先生，以及中日贸易协会理事油谷恭一先生。

大阪在代表团中的代表有：东京棉纺织株式会社总裁兼大日本棉纺织协会会长庄司乙吉先生、住友银行常务理事大平贤作先生，以及东兴纺绩织布株式会社总裁饭尾一二先生。

名古屋在代表团中的代表有：丰田棉纺绩织布株式会社总裁丰田利三郎先生。

代表团随行人员共七人。

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, MARCH 14, 1937 19058

Japanese Economic
Mission To China

This afternoon, the Japanese Economic Mission to
China, headed by Mr. Kodama, President of the Sino-
Japanese Trade Association and former President of the
Yokohama Specie Bank will arrive for a week's visit to
this country. We desire to take this early opportunity to
extend its members our sincere welcome.
China desires co-operation with Japan, provided it is
real and not nominal co-operation. For some years, the
relations between these two countries have not been
what they should be; and it is high time that these relations
be re-adjusted on an equitable and friendly basis.
We are very happy to hear the pronouncements of
Japan's new Foreign Minister, Mr. Sato. For if future
Japanese policy will be based on Mr. Sato's declarations, it
is felt that the day is not far away when these two major
Asiatic Powers will regain a normal relationship that is so
necessary for the happiness and prosperity of both.
China is always ready to respond to friendliness with
friendliness, frankness with frankness. Appreciating the
change of policy that is now being attempted at Tokyo,
Chinese leaders have not lagged behind in their earnest
efforts to bring about an atmosphere in which friendly dis-
cussions on economic co-operation between the financial and
industrial leaders of the two countries may be had.
The fundamental principle of economic co-operation be-
tween the two countries must be based on equality, mutual
respect, co-existence and co-prosperity.
From this principle the Chinese Government and people
will not, and cannot, depart.
We are not unaware of the declarations of Japan's
statesmen and financial leaders during recent months which
give recognition to this principle. It is fervently hoped
that such verbal recognition will soon find expression in
concrete action.
The coming of the Mission, we hope, will be the first
unofficial link of the chain that is to bring about real and
definite Sino-Japanese economic co-operation, which event-
ually will lead, in turn, to mutual political understanding.
We desire to wish the Mission success in this task for upon
it rests a great deal of responsibility for future relations,
political and economic, between the two countries.
In a special article in THE CHINA PRESS Weekly today,
we have dwelt in length on may points we consider as of
paramount importance. Some of the most essential may well
be recapitulated here:
Smuggling, drugging, and spying—that three-
headed snake that has been wiggling its way even across
the Yellow River. A halt must be called to this poisonous
policy, or there can be no economic co-operation. . . .
We are convinced of the sincerity of those Japanese
leaders who are now exerting all the efforts at their dispo-
sal to effect a reversal of Japan's previous policy. There-
fore, we wish to assure them that China will meet, as she
has always met in the past, Japan more than half way. In
this spirit of harmony, we hope that this Economic Mis-
sion from Japan will be the first link of a chain of co-operat-
ing activities that is yet to be forged and wish it success.
. . .
We desire co-operation with Japan. We want economic
co-operation with a country which is our closest neighbor.
We cannot, however, it must be remembered, accept co-opera-
tion on unilateral terms. As an indication of sincerity, the
Chinese people, it may be predicted, would not be unwilling
to treat Manchuria as a "suspense account." But under no
circumstances, this "suspense account" should be increased.
Rather, it should be gradually liquidated. Working towards
that ultimate liquidation, the multifarious illegitimate
activities of the Japanese subjects and their lackeys in North
China must be stopped, and stopped at once. To evade
responsibility by the Japanese authorities is an indication of
insincerity. For the consensus of opinion, foreign or
Chinese, is that it is absolutely within their power to stop
those activities—activities that have created the East Hopei
Force, the Smuggling Fraternity, the Narcotic Invasion, and
the so-called "special" but in reality espionage organizations.
The Chinese are not unaware of the conditions that have
prevailed in Japan for the last ten years. And they fully
realize that three months, or even three years, cannot
possibly transform that militaristic, aggressive, "con-
tinental" outlook held by so many Japanese expansionists
and deliberately imposed upon their people. All that the
Chinese people dare to hope for is a right beginning in the
right direction. No doubt, many of us are placing in the
coming of the Economic Mission as an indication of the
change of heart as well as the change of policy. . . .

（批：S.R 14/3）

《字林西报》，1937年3月14日，星期日 19058

日本经济代表团访华

今天下午，由中日贸易协会理事长、前横滨正金银行总裁儿玉先生（Mr. Kodama）率领的日本经济代表团将抵达本国，进行为期一周的访问。我们要借此早期机会，向该团成员表示我们诚挚的欢迎。

中国希望与日本合作，前提是这种合作是真实的而非名义上的。多年来，两国关系并未达到应有的状态；现在是时候在公平友好的基础上重新调整这些关系了。

我们很高兴听到日本新任外相佐藤先生（Mr. Sato）的声明。因为如果日本未来的政策基于佐藤先生的宣言，那么人们认为，这两个亚洲大国恢复对双方幸福与繁荣如此必要的正常关系之日已不远矣。

中国总是准备以友好回应友好，以坦诚回应坦诚。鉴于东京方面正在尝试改变政策，中国领导人在营造一种氛围方面并未落后，在这种氛围中，两国的金融和工业领袖可以就经济合作进行友好讨论。

两国经济合作的基本原则必须建立在平等、相互尊重、共存与共荣的基础上。

中国政府和人民不会、也不能背离这一原则。

我们并非不知道日本政治家和金融领袖在最近几个月的声明中承认了这一原则。我们热切希望这种口头上的承认能很快转化为具体的行动。

我们希望，代表团的到来将成为促成真正且明确的中日经济合作链条中的第一个非官方环节，而这最终又将导致相互的政治谅解。我们祝愿代表团在此项任务中取得成功，因为两国未来的政治和经济关系在很大程度上取决于此。

在今日《字林西报》周刊的一篇特别文章中，我们详细阐述了我们认为至关重要的许多观点。其中一些最核心的要点不妨在此重述：

走私、贩毒和间谍活动——这条三头蛇甚至已蜿蜒爬过黄河。必须叫停这种有毒的政策，否则就不可能有经济合作……

我们相信那些日本领袖的诚意，他们正竭尽全力扭转日本以往的政策。因此，我们要向他们保证，中国将像过去一贯所做的那样，对日本做出超过半数的让步。本着这种和谐的精神，我们希望来自日本的这个经济代表团将成为尚未锻造而成的合作活动链条中的第一环，并祝愿其成功。

……

我们希望与日本合作。我们希望与作为我们最近邻的国家进行经济合作。然而，必须记住，我们不能接受单方面的合作。作为诚意的表示，可以预测，中国人民并不反对将满洲视为“悬账”。但在任何情况下，这笔“悬账”都不应增加。相反，它应逐渐清算。为了实现最终的清算，必须立即停止日本臣民及其在北方的走狗的各种非法活动。日本当局推卸责任是不诚意的表现。因为无论外国舆论还是中国舆论的一致看法是，制止这些活动完全在他们的能力范围内——这些活动造就了冀东部队、走私集团、毒品入侵以及所谓的“特殊”实则间谍组织。

中国人并非不了解过去十年在日本盛行的状况。他们充分认识到，三个月，甚至三年，都不可能彻底改变许多日本扩张主义者所持有并刻意强加给其人民的军国主义、侵略性的“大陆”观念。中国人民敢于希望的只是一个朝着正确方向的正确开端。毫无疑问，我们许多人将经济代表团的到来视为心意转变以及政策改变的标志……

（批注：S.R 14/3）

NO. 11.
Registered at the Chinese Post
Office as Newspaper
Sunday, March 14, 1937
no-Japanese Economic Co-operation
—By C. KUANGSON YOUNG—
Managing-Director, China Press
In the afternoon of March 14, the Shanghai Maru will be bringing from Japan to this country the Japanese Economic Mission, headed by Mr. Kenji Kodama, former President of the Yokohama Specie Bank. Although denying that the Mission has been entrusted with any important, special, or definite “mission”, he declared some days ago that it would “doubtless prepare the ground for economic co-operation between China and Japan.”
Mr. Toyotaro Yuki, before his assumption of the important post of Minister of Finance, declared during January that the purpose of the Mission was twofold:
First, it would return the courtesy call of the Chinese Industrial Mission which visited Japan in 1935, and,
Secondly, it would take the opportunity to impress upon Chinese official and private circles Japan’s side of the argument for the joint development of China’s economic resources.
* * *
We are pleased to see that the Mission is composed of leaders of unquestionable prominence in the financial and industrial fields of Japan. Chosen by the Sino-Japanese Trade Association, the list includes, in addition to the chief of the mission who as mentioned above is Mr. K. Kodama, President of the Sino-Japanese Trade Association of Japan and former President of the Yokohama Specie Bank, such men of note as the following:
Mr. I. Iiwo Vice-President of the Sino-Japanese Trade Association of Japan and Director of the Japanese Cotton Mills Owners Association in China.
Mr. M. Miyake Adviser of the Mitsubishi Shoji Kaisha and Director of the Sino-Japanese Trade Association.
Mr. M. Kato President of the Bank of Chosen.
Mr. O. Shoji President of the Toyo Cotton Spinning Company, Managing-Director of Dai Nippon Cotton, Spinning and Weaving Mills Association, and Director of the Sino-Japanese Trade Association.
Mr. N. Ohtani President of Nippon Yussen Kaisha, and Director of the Sino-Japanese Trade Association.
Mr. S. Miyajima President of Nisshin Spinning and Weaving Company and Director of the Sino-Japanese Trade Association.
Mr. K. Ohira Director of the Sumitomo Bank.
Mr. S. Hori President of Nisshin Kisen Kaisha and Director of the Sino-Japanese Trade Association.
Mr. R. Toyoda President of the Toyoda Cotton, Spinning and Weaving Co.
Mr. R. Ishida Managing Director of Mitsui Bussan Kaisha.
Mr. A. Fujiyama President of Dai Nippon Sugar Manufacturing Company.
Mr. A. Akiyama Counsellor of Mitsubishi Trading Co.
Mr. K. Aburatani Director of the Sino-Japanese Trade Association.
* * *
As the Japanese leaders, since December last, have profusely indicated through public pronouncements their determined desire to revise their views regarding China and re-orientate their foreign policy accordingly, the Chinese are ready to readjust their hopes and outlook on the possibility of Sino-Japanese economic co-operation.

第11期
在中国邮局注册为报纸
1937年3月14日，星期日
中日经济合作
——作者：C. KUANGSON YOUNG——
《字林西报》总经理

3月14日下午，“上海丸”号（Shanghai Maru）将把由前横滨正金银行总裁儿玉健二先生（Mr. Kenji Kodama）率领的日本经济代表团从日本带至本国。尽管否认该代表团被赋予任何重要、特殊或明确的“使命”，但他几天前宣称，此举“无疑将为中日经济合作奠定基础”。

结城丰太郎先生（Mr. Toyotaro Yuki）在就任财政大臣这一重要职位之前，曾于一月份声明，代表团的目的是双重的：

第一，回访1935年访问日本的中国工业代表团；
第二，借此机会向中国官方和民间各界灌输日本关于共同开发中国经济资源的论点。

* * *

我们很高兴看到，该代表团由日本金融和工业界无可争议的杰出领袖组成。由中日贸易协会选出的名单包括，除了上述代表团团长、日本中日贸易协会理事长兼前横滨正金银行总裁儿玉健二先生（K. Kodama）之外，还有以下知名人士：

I. Iiwo 先生，日本中日贸易协会副理事长，在华日本棉纺厂主协会董事。
M. Miyake 先生，三菱商事会社顾问，中日贸易协会董事。
M. Kato 先生，朝鲜银行总裁。
O. Shoji 先生，东洋棉花株式会社总裁，大日本棉花纺织织造协会总经理，中日贸易协会董事。
N. Ohtani 先生，日本邮船会社总裁，中日贸易协会董事。
S. Miyajima 先生，日清纺织织造公司总裁，中日贸易协会董事。
K. Ohira 先生，住友银行董事。
S. Hori 先生，日清汽船会社总裁，中日贸易协会董事。
R. Toyoda 先生，丰田棉花纺织织造公司总裁。
R. Ishida 先生，三井物产会社总经理。
A. Fujiyama 先生，大日本制糖会社总裁。
A. Akiyama 先生，三菱贸易公司参事。
K. Aburatani 先生，中日贸易协会董事。

* * *

鉴于日本领导人自去年十二月以来通过公开声明大量表明了其修改对华观点并据此调整外交政策的坚定愿望，中国人已准备好重新调整他们对中日经济合作可能性的希望和展望。

pages.en:
On this occasion, therefore, of the visit of these Japanese financial and industrial leaders, we desire to extend them our sincere welcome; we receive them with open arms as well as an open mind.
Co-operation, economic or otherwise, between these two or other countries, must be built on the principle of reciprocity, equality, mutuality, co-existence and co-prosperity.
It is this principle, and this principle alone, that can bring about success.
* * *
Japan must congratulate herself on securing the services of Finance Minister Yuki and Foreign Minister Sato. In their policy, one sees the light of Far Eastern peace. If their policy can be executed in its entirety, without hindrance or interference from quarters described by Mr. Sato himself as “dual” control, there is no reason why China and Japan, the two major Powers of Asia, cannot come together in the interest of their economic prosperity and political stability.
The idea that Japan, and Japan alone, is the stabilizing force of the Far East must be thrown overboard at once. For it is this arrogant, egoistic thesis that has almost catapulted this part of the world into a maelstrom of hatred, war, chaos. We are happy that Mr. Sato, a seasoned diplomat who has seen the world, has enough courage to discourage such studied superiority complex as hitherto entertained by Japanese diplomats in China, Japanese military men in North China, and many officials in Tokyo. In the words of Mr. Sato:
“In the diplomatic dealings of a nation, the importance of the ‘other party’ must not be forgotten. In the height of excitement, when strong words and views prevail, the very existence of the ‘other party’ is quite often unfortunately pushed back too far to the vanishing point.”
Continuing, the Foreign Minister pointed out, clearly and emphatically, the fallacy of pressure without limit.
“There had been too often the incorrect impression that with sufficient pressure, any demand, no matter in what form or of what nature, may be forced down the throat of the other party in docile submission. Such a view excluded entirely the possibility of popular reaction which would render a diplomatic stalemate inevitable, to the detriment of both parties.”
* * *
China is ready to co-operate with, but she unquestionably will resist being operated upon by, Japan. No words are necessary to explain this policy of China. It has already been pointed out previously that the kind of economic “cooperation” as now forced down the throat of North China, is not the brand which the Chinese people can be expected to welcome or tolerate.
Smuggling, drugging, and spying—that three-headed snake that has been wiggling its way even across the Yellow River. A halt must be called to this poisonous policy, or there can be no economic cooperation.
And we are certain this North China brand is not the brand which the visiting Economic Mission to China, the new Foreign Minister Mr. Sato, or the Finance Minister Mr. Yuki, has in mind.
We are convinced of the sincerity of those Japanese leaders who are now exerting all the efforts at their disposal to effect a reversal of Japan’s previous policy. Therefore, we wish to assure them that China will meet, as she has always met in the past, Japan more than half way. In this spirit of harmony, we hope that this Economic Mission from Japan will be the first link of a chain of co-operating activities that is yet to be forged and wish it success.
* * *
The Chinese people are among those who are ready to respond with frankness when approached with frankness, to treat with sincerity when they are treated with sincerity. They continue to hold reasonable views even in times of either anger or distress if they are assured of similar reasonableness on the part of those with whom they have to deal. It is no exaggeration to say that the utterances of those Japanese leaders who have since December urged the necessity of a new China policy for Japan have made a deeper impression on this side of the Yellow and Japan Seas rather than on the other.
We desire co-operation with Japan. We want economic cooperation with a country which is our closest neighbor. We cannot, however, it must be remembered, accept coopera-
pages.zh:
因此，值此日本金融和工业领袖来访之际，我们要向他们表示诚挚的欢迎；我们以开放的胸怀和开放的心态接待他们。

这两国或其他国家之间的合作，无论是经济还是其他方面，都必须建立在互惠、平等、互助、共存与共荣的原则之上。

只有这一原则，唯有这一原则，才能带来成功。

* * *

日本应当庆幸自己拥有了财政大臣结城和外相佐藤的服务。在他们的政策中，人们看到了远东和平的光芒。如果他们的政策能够完整执行，而不受佐藤先生本人所称的“双重”控制部门的阻碍或干涉，那么没有理由认为，作为亚洲两大强国的中国和日本不能为了其经济繁荣和政治稳定而走到一起。

日本、且唯有日本是远东稳定力量的想法必须立即抛弃。因为正是这种傲慢、自私的论调，几乎将世界这部分地区推入了仇恨、战争和混乱的漩涡。我们很高兴看到，佐藤先生这位阅历丰富的资深外交官，有足够的勇气去抑制此前日本驻华外交官、华北日军军官以及东京许多官员所抱有的那种精心培养的优越感情结。用佐藤先生的话说：

“在一个国家的外交交往中，绝不能忘记‘对方’的重要性。在情绪高涨、强硬言辞和观点占上风的时候，‘对方’的存在往往不幸地被推得太远，直至消失点。”

外相接着清楚而 emphatically 地指出了无限施压的谬误。

“人们常常有一种错误的印象，认为只要有足够的压力，任何要求，无论形式如何或性质如何，都可以强行塞入对方的喉咙，使其顺从地接受。这种观点完全排除了民众反应的可能性，而这种反应将使外交僵局不可避免，从而损害双方利益。”

* * *

中国准备与日本合作，但她毫无疑问将抵抗被日本操纵。无需多言来解释中国的这一政策。此前已指出，目前强加于华北的那种经济“合作”，并不是中国人民所期望欢迎或容忍的那一类。

走私、贩毒和间谍活动——这条三头蛇甚至已蜿蜒爬过黄河。必须叫停这种有毒的政策，否则就不可能有经济合作。

而且我们确信，这种华北品牌并不是来访的中国经济代表团、新任外相佐藤先生或财政大臣结城先生心中所想的品牌。

我们相信那些日本领袖的诚意，他们正竭尽全力扭转日本以往的政策。因此，我们要向他们保证，中国将像过去一贯所做的那样，对日本做出超过半数的让步。本着这种和谐的精神，我们希望来自日本的这个经济代表团将成为尚未锻造而成的合作活动链条中的第一环，并祝愿其成功。

* * *

中国人民属于那些当以坦诚相待时便以坦诚回应、当以真诚相待时便以真诚相处的人之一。如果确信与之打交道的一方也表现出同样的理性，即使在愤怒或困苦时期，他们仍持合理的观点。毫不夸张地说，自去年十二月以来敦促日本实行新对华政策的那些日本领导人的言论，在黄海和日本海的这一侧比在另一侧留下了更深刻的印象。

我们希望与日本合作。我们希望与作为我们最近邻的国家进行经济合作。然而，必须记住，我们不能接受合

pages.en:
tion on unilateral terms. As an indication of sincerity, the
Chinese people, it may be predicted, would not be unwilling
to treat Manchuria as a "suspense account." But under no
circumstances, this "suspense account" should be increased.
Rather, it should be gradually liquidated. Working towards
that ultimate liquidation, the multifarious illegitimate
activities of the Japanese subjects and their lackeys in North
China must be stopped, and stopped at once. To evade
responsibility by the Japanese authorities is an indication of
insincerity. For the concensus of opinion, foreign or
Chinese, is that it is absolutely within their power to stop
those activities—activities that have created the East Hopei
Farce, the Smuggling Fraternity, the Narcotic Invasion, and
the so-called "special" but in reality espionage organizations.
The Chinese are not unaware of the conditions that have
prevailed in Japan for the last ten years. And they fully
realize that three months, or even three years, cannot
possibly transform that militaristic, aggressive, "con-
tinental" outlook held by so many Japanese expansionists
and deliberately imposed upon their people. All that the
Chinese people dare to hope for is a right beginning in the
right direction. No doubt, many of us are placing in the
coming of the Economic Mission as an indication of the
change of heart as well as the change of policy.
* * *
Ambassador Kawagoe it was who fired the first shot
that burst Japan's balloon of self-complacency and self-
deceit. To him, both countries must be grateful for the
improved atmosphere that will make further improvement
possible. He it was who in his first interview to the press
at the beginning of December, after an eighty-three day
sojourn in Nanking where he unsuccessfully conducted the
Sino-Japanese negotiations on the basis of the old policy,
declared that Japan must acquire a new concept of modern
China if the two nations are to come to an understanding.
Continuing he said:
"My own opinion on China has changed after my transfer
South from the North and I have acquired a number of new
ideas as the result of my stay in Nanking.
"I am firmly convinced that Japan should render full honors
to the devotion to duty of certain Chinese officials, especially
the younger ones."
Supporting the Ambassador's views, the Shanghai
Nippo, a local Japanese newspaper, on December 7 editorially
urged the Japanese Government to abandon its "old-fashion-
ed" policy towards this country. The paper said that no
progress would be made in the readjustment of Sino-Japan-
ese relations until the Japanese people change their concep-
tion of China and realize the tremendous changes that had
taken place in this country after the formation of the
National Government in Nanking in 1927. The Nippo con-
tinued:
"The application of such terms as 'the old country' or 'the
sleeping lion' to China is no longer advisable. China is rapidly
becoming a modern, unified state, totally different from China
of ten years ago.
"Real rapprochement between the two countries must be
based on a realization of this change. Unfortunately, too often
we base our opinions on the views of the so-called 'old China-
hands.'
"When one arrives in Nanking he is immediately struck by
something that he does not sense in Shanghai, Peiping or Canton.
This can possibly be the earnestness exhibited by the Nanking
officialdom.
"We must admit that China has made great gains in her
unification under Gen. Chiang Kai-shek."
* * *
A month later, the Japanese Ambassador, in an exclusive
interview to the Nanking correspondent of the Tokyo Asahi
stated:
"China's rapid strides towards the goal of a truly modern
state may be evidenced by her efforts at economic recon-
struction of the country, and the whole-hearted support of
the Chinese people to their Government."
Comparing China at the present moment to Japan
during the Meiji renaissance, Mr. Kawagoe paid a glowing
tribute to the "really commendable spirit" of the entire
Chinese nation, including the officialdom, the soldiery and
the common mass, in their united effort to re-vitalize the
country.
At the end of January, the Nippo pointed out
that one of the major causes of the resignation of the Hirota
Cabinet was its "blundering diplomatic policy." Re-iterat-
ing its views as expressed previously, the editorial article
poignantly commented on the success with which Great
Britain had won China's confidence through her sincere
efforts in meeting China's needs and wishes. The Hayashi
Cabinet was urged to exhibit a "deeper understanding of
the actual situation in China, if it hopes to secure true rap-
prochement between the two nations".
* * *
pages.zh:
在单方面条款基础上的……（原文此处残缺）。作为诚意的表示，可以预见，中国人民不会不愿意将满洲问题视为一个“悬案”。但在任何情况下，这个“悬案”都不应扩大。相反，它应逐渐得到解决。为了实现最终的解决，必须立即停止日本臣民及其在华华北地区的走狗所进行的各种非法活动。日本当局推卸责任，表明其缺乏诚意。因为无论外国舆论还是中国舆论的共识是：他们完全有能力制止这些活动——正是这些活动制造了冀东伪政权闹剧、走私集团、毒品入侵以及所谓“特殊”实则从事间谍活动的组织。中国人民并非不了解过去十年间日本国内的状况。他们充分认识到，三个月，甚至三年，都不可能改变许多日本扩张主义者所持有并刻意强加于其民众身上的那种军国主义、侵略性的“大陆”观念。中国人民所敢希望的，只是一个朝着正确方向迈出的良好开端。毫无疑问，我们许多人将日本经济使团的到来视为其心态转变以及政策改变的标志。
* * *
正是川越茂大使打响了第一枪，戳破了日本自满和自欺的气球。两国都应当感谢他改善了氛围，从而使进一步的改善成为可能。正是在十二月初，他在南京逗留八十三天、基于旧政策进行的日中谈判无功而返后，于首次接受记者采访时宣称，如果两国要达成谅解，日本必须获得对现代中国的新概念。他接着说：
“我自北方调任南方后，我对中国的看法发生了改变，在南京逗留期间，我产生了一些新想法。
“我坚信，日本应当充分尊重某些中国官员，尤其是年轻官员的敬业精神。”
支持大使观点的是上海当地日文报纸《上海日报》（Shanghai Nippo），该报于12月7日发表社论，敦促日本政府放弃对这个国家的“过时”政策。该报称，在日本人民改变对中国的观念，并认识到1927年南京国民政府成立后该国发生的巨大变化之前，中日关系的调整不会取得任何进展。《上海日报》继续写道：
“将‘古老国度’或‘睡狮’等术语用于中国已不再适宜。中国正迅速成为一个现代化的统一国家，与十年前的中国截然不同。
“两国之间真正的亲善必须建立在对这一变化的认识之上。不幸的是，我们往往过于依赖所谓‘中国通’的观点来形成我们的看法。
“当一个人抵达南京时，他会立即感受到一种在上海、北平或广州所感觉不到的东西。这可能是南京官场表现出的 earnestness（热忱/认真）。
“我们必须承认，中国在蒋介石将军领导下实现了巨大的统一成果。”
* * *
一个月后，日本大使在接受东京《朝日新闻》南京特派记者的独家专访时表示：
“中国朝着真正现代化国家目标迈进的快速步伐，可以从其国家经济重建的努力以及中国人民对其政府的全心支持中得到证明。”
川越先生将当下的中国与明治维新时期的日本相提并论，对整个中华民族——包括官场、军队和普通民众——在振兴国家的共同努力中所表现出的“真正值得称赞的精神”给予了高度赞扬。
一月底，《上海日报》指出，广田内阁辞职的主要原因之一是其“笨拙的外交政策”。该社论重申了此前表达的观点，尖锐地评论了英国通过真诚努力满足中国的需求和愿望从而赢得中国信任的成功。文章敦促林铣十郎内阁表现出“对中国实际情况的更深刻理解”，如果它希望确保两国之间真正的亲善关系的话。
* * *

pages.en:
Following the footsteps of Ambassador Kawagoe and
the Nippo Editor, Mr. Yoshida, Chairman of the Japanese
Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Shanghai and Man-
ager of the Shanghai Branch of the Mitsubishi Bank came
out with candid, frank, helpful views regarding this country.
"The National Government of China," stated the banker
in a pamphlet widely distributed to the business and financial
circles of Tokyo, "is now completely secure, with capable hands
in control of the nation's finances and economy. . . .
"Japan has always thought that the National Government
will rise or fall with the so-called Kiangsu and Chekiang
financiers, but now the Government is closely tied with the
economic interests of the entire nation, which is a phenomenon
unprecedented in Chinese history . . .
"Japan has always thought that China lacks unity and
that the Chinese people are as incohesive as sand, but now the
sand is hardening like cement, which is a logical reaction to
the pressure applied by Japan and other countries. . . ."
Pointing to the smuggling situation in North China and
Japan's unfriendly attitude towards China's currency re-
forms, the Shanghai Japanese banker said these were not
measures conducive to Sino-Japanese economic co-operation.
* * *
The cause that has been sponsored by Ambasador
Kawagoe, the Nippo, and Mr. Yoshida is evidently bearing
fruit. Preceding the arrival of Japan's Economic Mission to
China, the Federation of Japanese Chambers of Commerce
in China held its first meeting on Thursday. The Con-
ference is the second of its kind, the first having been held
some fifteen years ago.
Attending the Conference are forty representatives
from the eight Japanese Chambers of Commerce of Shang-
hai, Hankow, Tientsin, Tsingtao, Tsinan, Peiping, Dairen and
Hongkong. Mr. Yoshida, President of the Conference, in-
formed the CHINA PRESS that the purpose of the Conference
was to devise ways and means to improve and maintain
friendly relations between the two countries and to reach
an economic understanding of benefit to both.
* * *
The fact that for fifteen years there has been no co-
ordinating effort on the part of the Japanese business men
in China and that such a conference should be held at this
moment give us encouragement that perhaps, in the near
future, a new path will be opened for Sino-Japanese eco-
nomic and business relations. We desire to call attention
especially to Mr. Yoshida's remarks, made during his speech
at the Conference Banquet Friday evening:
"How to improve and maintain friendly relations between
the two countries is the most important question of the day.
We business men must make efforts to bring about economic
co-operation.
"For that purpose, we must have a correct knowledge and
understanding of the necessity for economic co-operation.
"China is making great progress in her national unification,
both politically and economically. To carry on this unification,
it may be necessary to have foreign assistance, more or less.
However, what I am afraid of is that if the relation between
China and Japan is not harmonious, China's seeking assistance
from any foreign country is liable to be very dangerous to
both countries."
Not only those who have direct contact with China have
changed their opinion, concept, ideas about this country, its
officialdom and people. Leaders in Japan have begun to
realize the situation; and what is more important, they have
come out in the open to inform their people. First among
these was Prince Konoye, President of the House of Peers,
who in a vigorous article at the beginning of January in the
Osaka Asahi advocated mutual respect and sympathy
between the two nations.
Declaring that Japan's relations with China constitute
the crux of her foreign policy, the aged statesman called
attention to Tokyo's failure in effecting the desired rap-
prochement because of the "unwholesome" view it held of
this country. Such a view precluded the possibility of
handling the issues with dexterity and propriety by the
Tokyo Government. He stated:
"Both sides should extend their hand of cooperation from
the standpoint of their own fatherland and our aim is to
develop the Chinese people's love for China and the Japanese
people's love for Japan into a larger and mutual love for the
entire Asiatic race."
pages.zh:
紧随川越大使和《上海日报》编辑吉田先生的脚步，上海日本商工会议所会长兼三菱银行上海分行经理吉田先生就这个国家发表了坦率、直率且有益的看法。这位银行家在向东京商界和金融界广泛分发的小册子中 stated（陈述）：“中国国民政府现在完全稳固，国家财政和经济由能干的人士掌控……
“日本一直认为，国民政府的兴衰取决于所谓的江苏和浙江金融家，但现在政府与全国的经济利益紧密相连，这是中国历史上前所未有的现象……
“日本一直认为中国缺乏统一，中国人民像沙子一样松散，但现在沙子正像水泥一样硬化，这是对日本和其他国家施加压力的逻辑反应……”
这位上海日本银行家指出华北的走私局势以及日本对中国货币改革的不友好态度，称这些都不是有利于中日经济合作的措施。
* * *
由川越大使、《上海日报》和吉田先生所倡导的事业显然正在结出果实。在日本经济使团抵达中国之前，在华日本商工会议所联合会于周四举行了首次会议。这是第二次此类会议，第一次是在大约十五年前举行的。
出席会议的有来自上海、汉口、天津、青岛、济南、北平、大连和香港八个日本商工会议所的四十名代表。会议主席吉田先生告诉《字林西报》（CHINA PRESS），会议的目的是制定改善和维持两国友好关系的方法，并达成对双方都有利的经济谅解。
* * *
事实上，在华日本商人十五年来一直没有协调行动，而在此时举行这样的会议，令我们感到鼓舞，也许在不久的将来，中日经济和商务关系将开辟一条新的道路。我们要特别提请注意吉田先生在周五晚间的会议宴会演讲中所说的话：
“如何改善和维持两国的友好关系是当今最重要的问题。我们商界人士必须努力促成经济合作。
“为此，我们必须正确认识和了解经济合作的必要性。
“中国在政治和经济方面的国家统一方面取得了巨大进步。为了推进这种统一，可能在一定程度上需要外国的援助。然而，我担心的是，如果中日关系不和谐，中国向任何外国寻求援助都可能对两国非常危险。”
不仅那些与中国有直接接触的人改变了他们对这个国家、其官场和人民的看法、观念和想法。日本的领导人也开始意识到局势；更重要的是，他们公开向其民众通报情况。其中第一位是贵族院议长近卫文麿公爵，他在一月初的大阪《朝日新闻》上发表了一篇有力的文章，倡导两国之间的相互尊重和同情。
这位资深政治家宣称，日本与中国的关系构成了其外交政策的关键，并提请人们注意，东京未能实现预期的亲善关系，是因为其对这个国家持有“不健康”的看法。这种观点使得东京政府无法灵活且得体地处理这些问题。他 stated（陈述）：
“双方都应从各自祖国的立场出发伸出合作之手，我们的目标是将中国人民对中国的爱和日本人民对日本的爱，发展为对整个亚洲种族更大范围的互爱。”

pages.en:
* * *
Even before his acceptance of the financial portfolio,
Mr. Yuki as the new President of the Chamber of Commerce
and Industry of Tokyo urged "self-restraint" as Japan's
policy towards China; for, self-restraint would be an im-
portant factor in bringing about Sino-Japanese economic
rapprochement. Mr. Yuki informed the leading ministers
of the defunct Hirota cabinet that the Chamber desired
sincerely a general readjustment of Sino-Japanese relations,
for such readjustment would result in the stabilization of
the conditions in the Orient and bring about prosperity for
both nations.
Such outspoken views, may it be emphasized, are very
much appreciated by the bankers and industrialists of this
country, who are genuinely desirous of cooperation. But so
far, their desire has been frustrated by adverse developments
over which the Japanese authorities, to a large measure,
have control.
* * *
The Hayashi Cabinet has given us encouragement, for
Premier Hayashi himself, War Minister Sugiyama, Finance
Minister Yuki and Foreign Minister Sato have all publicly
made statements which are calculated to improve the rela-
tions between these two countries.
Before the Budget Committee of the Lower House on
February 20, Premier Hayashi indicated the decision of the
Japanese Government to change its China policy. The new
Japanese policy would concentrate on the promotion of
cultural relations, "based on the fact that Japan in no
circumstances seeks to acquire any portion of Chinese ter-
ritory." Echoing the Premier's pronouncement, General
Sugiyama, Minister of War, pointed out the Empire's lack
of territorial ambitions on the Asiatic continent. He said
that the Government was convinced that Sino-Japanese
relationship might be improved through economic coopera-
tion and was straining every effort in that direction.
* * *
The reception by the Japanese and Chinese alike to
Mr. Yuki's appointment to the head the Finance Ministry
indicated the general feeling prevalent that his views were
the correct views for these two countries to follow. An
equally happy reaction was noticeable to Mr. Sato's declara-
tion of a "New Deal" China Policy. Although some reports
were current that it was received with reserve in Nanking,
such reserve was caused by the fear that the policy, as
declared, might not be able to go farther than the Diet
where it was announced.
Therefore, all the heavier is the responsibility of the
distinguished visitors to this country. They must realize
this visit is more than a courtesy visit. On this visit
depends much of the future course of Sino-Japanese rela-
tions, economic and political. If they are in agreement—
and they cannot but be in agreement—with the views as
expressed by the leaders of their government, of commerce
and industry in Japan as well as in China, they must leave
no stone unturned to overthrow the ideas and tactics
formerly entertained and employed by such men as their
notorious "Lawrence of Manchuria" and his kind. They
must take positive measures to assist their Government to
batter down all opposition and carry out without any mental
reservation the new China Policy.
* * *
On the part of China, she will be, as she has always
been, ready to cooperate with nations that are friendly to
her, without ulterior motives.
We may conclude in the words of Dr. Wang Chung-
hui, China's new Foreign Minister, who said in his inter-
view to the press a few days ago:
"Guided by the fixed policy of the Government and the
principles of international justice, I shall endeavor, in strict
accordance with diplomatic usage, to secure the realization of
the aspirations of the Chinese Government and the develop-
ment through international co-operation of the relations
between China and foreign powers to the benefit of all con-
cerned."
pages.zh:
* * *
甚至在就任财政大臣之前，东京商工会议所新任会长结城（Yuki）先生便敦促将“克制”作为日本对华政策；因为，克制将是促成中日经济缓和的重要因素。结城先生告知已解散的广田内阁的主要阁员，商工会议所真诚希望全面调整中日关系，因为这种调整将导致东方局势的稳定，并为两国带来繁荣。
必须强调，这种坦率的观点深受本国银行家和实业家的赞赏，他们真心渴望合作。但迄今为止，他们的愿望因不利的局势发展而受挫，而在很大程度上，日本当局对这些发展拥有控制权。
* * *
林内阁给了我们鼓励，因为林首相本人、陆军大臣杉山、财政大臣结城和外相佐藤都公开发表了旨在改善两国关系的声明。
2月20日，在众议院预算委员会面前，林首相表明了日本政府改变对华政策的决定。新的日本政策将集中于促进文化关系，“基于日本在任何情况下都不寻求获取中国任何领土这一事实”。呼应首相的声明，陆军大臣杉山将军指出帝国在亚洲大陆没有领土野心。他说，政府确信通过经济合作可以改善中日关系，并正为此方向竭尽全力。
* * *
日本人和中国人对结城先生出任大藏省（财政部）长官的反应表明，普遍的感觉是他的观点是这两国应遵循的正确观点。对于佐藤先生宣布的“新政”对华政策，也出现了同样令人满意的反应。尽管有报告称南京方面对此持保留态度，但这种保留是由于担心所宣布的政策可能无法超越在其宣布地——国会——的范围。
因此，各位贵宾访问本国的责任更加重大。他们必须认识到，这次访问不仅仅是一次礼节性访问。中日关系未来的经济和政治走向在很大程度上取决于此次访问。如果他们同意——而且他们不得不同意——日本以及中国的政府、商业和工业领袖所表达的观点，他们就必须不遗余力地推翻像臭名昭著的“满洲的劳伦斯”及其同类人物以前所持有和采用的想法与策略。他们必须采取积极措施协助其政府打破所有反对意见，并无任何心理保留地执行新的对华政策。
* * *
就中国而言，她将一如既往，准备与对她友好、没有 ulterior motives（别有用心/其他动机）的国家进行合作。
我们可以用中国新任外交部长王宠惠博士几天前在接受记者采访时的话作为总结：
“在政府既定政策和国际正义原则的指导下，我将严格依照外交惯例，努力确保实现中国政府的愿望，并通过国际合作发展中国与外国列强之间的关系，以造福所有相关方。”

19888
THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, MARCH 12, 1937

Japanese Economic Mission
Starts On Journey Here
Chief Delegate Says Mission Will Make Every
Effort For Rapprochement On Basis Of Sino-
Japanese Equality And Reciprocity

TOKYO, March 11.—Elimination of existing Sino-Japanese antagonism is a prerequisite for the inauguration of economic co-operation between the two nations, Mr. Kenji Kodama, head of the economic mission to China, said to-day on his departure for Kobe.
To-morrow, Mr. Kodama and the other members of the mission will board the s.s. Nagasaki Maru, arriving in Shanghai two days later.
Mr. Kodama, who once headed the Yokohama Specie Bank, told the press he would exert every effort to bring about Sino-Japanese rapprochement on the basis of equality and reciprocity, as well as respect for China's territorial integrity.

He regretted the antagonistic feeling between the two peoples which, he said, had been the result of various Sino-Japanese political issues of recent years.
"The close nature of the relations between the two nations," he went on, "tends to cause frequent cases of friction, both political and economic.
Far-Sighted View Wanted
"It is incumbent upon the two great nations of the Far East to re-establish friendly relations by taking a far-sighted view of the situation and seeking a way out of the present difficulty, which will find its own solution if mutual understanding and reliance is fostered between them."
Mr. Kodama said that the mission will attend the first meeting of the Shanghai Sino-Japanese Association, formed in 1935, and will take advantage of the visit to inspect the economic and financial rehabilitation of China and exchange views with Chinese leaders.
The mission includes the following: Mr. Noboru Otani, President of the Nippon Yusen Kaisha; Mr. Keizaburo Kato, President of the Bank of Chosen; Mr. Hyakutaro Miyakegawa, adviser to the Mitsubishi Trading Company; Mr. Reisuke Ishida, managing director of the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha.
Others are: Mr. Akiyoshi Akiyama, adviser to the Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha; Mr. Arata Hori, President of the Nisshin Kisen Kaisha; Mr. Kyoichi Yutani, Director of the Sino-Japanese Businessmen's Association, and two or three Osaka industrialists.—Domei.

Nanking Preparations
NANKING, March 11.—Preparations have been completed here for the reception of the Japanese Economic Mission which is due to arrive in Nanking on March 15 for a three-day visit.
Among the high Government officials who will act as hosts at dinners and other functions include Mr. Wu Ting-chang, Minister of Industry; Dr. Wang Chung-hui, Minister of Communications, Mr. Chang Kia-ngau, Minister of Railways; and Dr. H. H. Kung, Minister of Finance.
—Central News.

19888
《上海泰晤士报》，1937年3月12日，星期五

日本经济代表团
启程来沪
首席代表称代表团将竭力在平等互惠基础上促成和解

东京，3月11日电。— 赴华经济代表团团长儿玉健二（Kenji Kodama）先生今日在启程前往神户时表示，消除现存的中日敌对情绪是启动两国经济合作的先决条件。
明日，儿玉先生及代表团其他成员将登上“长崎丸”号轮船，两天后抵达上海。
曾担任横滨正金银行行长的儿玉先生告诉新闻界，他将尽一切努力在平等、互惠以及尊重中国领土完整的基础上促成中日和解。

他对两国人民之间的敌对情绪表示遗憾，他说，这是近年来各种中日政治问题的结果。
“两国关系的密切性质，”他继续说道，“往往导致频繁的政治和经济摩擦。
需要远见卓识
“远东两大国有责任以远见的视角看待局势，寻求摆脱当前困境的途径，如果能在两者之间培养相互理解和信任，这种困境自会找到解决之道。”
儿玉先生说，代表团将出席1935年成立的上海中日协会的第一次会议，并将利用此次访问考察中国的经济和金融复兴情况，并与中国领导人交换意见。
代表团成员包括：日本邮船会社总裁大谷登（Noboru Otani）先生；朝鲜银行总裁加藤庆三郎（Keizaburo Kato）先生；三菱商事顾问三宅川百太郎（Hyakutaro Miyakegawa）先生；三井物产常务董事石田英助（Reisuke Ishida）先生。
其他成员包括：三菱合资公司顾问秋山明义（Akiyoshi Akiyama）先生；日清汽船株式会社总裁堀新（Arata Hori）先生；中日实业家联合会理事汤谷恭一（Kyoichi Yutani）先生，以及两三位大阪实业家。—同盟社。

南京方面的准备工作
南京，3月11日电。— 此处已完成接待日本经济代表团的准备工作，该团定于3月15日抵达南京，进行为期三天的访问。
将在晚宴和其他活动中担任东道主的高级政府官员包括：实业部部长吴鼎昌先生；交通部部长王宠惠博士；铁道部部长张嘉璈先生；以及财政部部长孔祥熙博士。
—中央通讯社。

February 1, 1937.

NICHI-NICHI

ARMED ROBBERS ACTIVE ON MILLER ROAD

Armed robberies have frequently
been reported on Miller Road. A large number of Japanese
live on this road. Are they simple cases of robbery
or are they acts of anti-Japanism? On the afternoon
of January 30 a Chinese suddenly appeared in Lane No.
788 Miller Road and levelled a pistol at another Chinese
who was walking in the lane. The latter shouted for
help whereupon the armed Chinese made good his escape.
The appearance of the man who was threatened by the armed
Chinese resembled that of a Japanese; he had evidently
been mistaken for one by the armed man.
At 5 p.m. the same day five
armed robbers attacked No. 25 Shh Chun Li, Miller Road,
a house occupied by Chinese, and carried off $77 in cash.

NIPPO

INAUGURATION OF SHANGHAI JAPANESE PEN CLUB

On the evening of January 30
several Japanese assembled at Mr. Takeuchi's home in
Dixwell Road Apartment and inaugurated the Shanghai Pen
Club. The new body will publish a magazine twice a year
in order to introduce China to Japanese by means of
short stories, novels, poems and translations of Chinese
literature. The first issue will appear at the end
of February and will be sold at $1 per copy. The
Uchiyama Book Store on North Szechuen Road will act as
agents.

SINO-JAPANESE RAPPROCHEMENT

The Nippo publishes the
following comment:-
The Sino-Japanese negotiations
are now at a standstill due to the present political
troubles in Japan and to the Sian incident in China.
We cannot foretell in what direction the relations
between Japan and China will develop after the formation
of a new Japanese Cabinet and the settlement of the Sian
trouble by Nanking.
Economically Japan and China
should approach each other closer.. In spite of the
political disputes between Japan and China, a Sino-
Japanese match manufacturing company has been organized
and will start business on February 1. This is due to
the fact that Chinese industrialists realize that Chinese
factories cannot compete with Japanese factories in China
because of lack of skilled workers and sound management.
Chinese industrialists are willing to co-operate with
Japanese industrialists, and leave all political matters
alone. If Japan desires to lead and co-operate with
China, this point must not be overlooked.
